check: correction: there IS a way to see the wall, but only as a developer preview
previousRoundSaid: There is no user-facing way to enable generation, based on searching the code for config files and commands.
correction: That was incomplete. The code has no such path - no config file, no command, and production=true is refused - but Gradle provides one: runWallPreview starts a real Minecraft client against an isolated directory with the fixture switched on.

runWallPreview.mainClass: net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClient, a real client rather than a headless server
runWallPreview.purposeField: the preview manifest it writes labels itself manual-client-preview-not-acceptance

whatItCanShow: A wall actually generating, in front of a human, which is exactly what the real-machine checklist lists as needing a person rather than a program.
constraintsThatKeepItFromBeingRealMachin: the directory must stay inside build/run, so it can never point at a real save
production stays false, so this is the isolated fixture path rather than the production path
the manifest records production false, isolatedFixture true and networkUsed false, and labels itself not acceptance
guardWorthNoting: prepareWallPreview refuses an existing directory that lacks the marker file, with the message 'Refusing an existing unmarked preview directory'. It will not adopt a directory it did not create.
whyTheCorrectionMatters: Saying there is no way to see the wall would have been wrong in a way that matters to the user: a developer preview exists and is the natural way to do the human visual check that remains NOT_RUN. The accurate statement is that there is no player-facing path and no acceptance path, but there is a preview path.
